LESSON: COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Comprehension. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What are the girls Subject-verb daily activities using correct oral sentences. holding?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. construct sentences on have been demonstrated by
2. recognise the correct use  Learners construct of subject-verb sentences using singular agreement to form and plural subjects for appropriate sentences, things at home and around
3. enjoy using indefinite teacher or from computing pronouns in their day to devices, and responds to day communication. questions based on indefinite pronouns
4. identify singular and plural plural forms of irregular plurals of irregular forms of irregular nouns for nouns. nouns e.g. effective oral communication, 
5. enjoy using ‘will’ by the teacher or from and ‘shall’ to computing devices, and communicate future respond to questions based time/intentions. on future time
6. identify the opposite of a sentences using the opposites group of words for of familiar and unfamiliar effective oral words communication, 

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Connected text means sentences and short passages — not only single words.

• First look at any new words. Then read the whole sentence.

• If you do not understand, read again more slowly and ask: Who? What? Where?

• Fluency grows when you re-read the same short passage until it sounds smooth.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about a child walking to school in Kenya. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 2: Time yourself reading a short passage. Read it again and try to sound clearer, not only faster.

Example 3: After reading, answer: Who was in the story? What happened first?

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read a short passage aloud to a partner. Ask them to tell you one clear sentence they heard.
2. Re-read the same passage silently, then aloud once more.
3. Write two questions about the passage and swap with a friend.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Read one short story or paragraph at home and retell it in four sentences.
2. List three new words from your reading and use each in a sentence.
3. Explain to a parent what the passage was mainly about.
